editors.name: Cursor AI Code Editor
editors.pricing_details: Free tier with 200 GPT-4o uses/month; Pro at $20/month for unlimited completions & Claude 3.5 Sonnet access.
editors.target_audience: Full-stack developers, AI enthusiasts, and engineers seeking high-speed AI inline refactoring
pros: Seamless fork of VS Code with full extension compatibility
Multi-file codebase indexing and context-aware edits (Cmd+K / Cmd+I)
Instant codebase search using vector embeddings
Integrates top models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and custom Cursor models
cons: Requires active subscription for unlimited high-tier model usage
Cloud-based indexing requires sending context snippets to remote servers (privacy concern for strict enterprise)
Can occasionally suggest overly eager changes across multiple files
editors.best_for: Developers who want cutting-edge AI pair programming directly inside a familiar VS Code environment.
editors.visual_theme: Modern sleek dark UI, pulsing neon blue code cursor, ambient dark grey glassmorphism workspace, illuminated floating AI prompt input overlay

editors.name: Visual Studio Code
editors.pricing_details: 100% Free for personal and commercial use.
editors.target_audience: Web, cloud, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and general multi-language developers
pros: Massive extension marketplace with thousands of free themes, linters, and plugins
Lightweight core startup with high customization capability
Built-in Git integration, terminal, and remote debugging (SSH / Containers)
Completely free with gigantic community support
cons: Electron-based app can consume significant RAM when loaded with heavy extensions
Out of the box experience requires installing extensions for specialized language support
Not a full zero-config IDE compared to JetBrains suites
editors.best_for: Every developer from beginners to seasoned pros who value versatility and an unmatched extension ecosystem.
editors.visual_theme: Classic dark blue theme, crisp sidebar file tree, terminal window split at bottom, colorful syntax highlighting with clean developer desk setup

editors.name: Zed Editor
editors.pricing_details: 100% Free open source code editor; opt-in paid team collaboration features planned.
editors.target_audience: Rust, C++, Web, and performance-focused developers demanding instant sub-millisecond typing response
pros: Written in Rust and GPUI rendered at 120+ FPS for blistering fast performance
Native multiplayer live-collaborative editing built into the core editor
Extremely low memory footprint and instant startup time
Built-in AI model support (Claude, OpenAI, Ollama local models)
cons: Smaller extension ecosystem compared to VS Code
Currently primary platform support focused on macOS and Linux (Windows in progress)
Less mature UI customization options
editors.best_for: Developers who prioritize raw typing performance, zero lag, and real-time team pairing.
editors.visual_theme: Minimalist dark slate editor workspace, ultra-smooth 120hz scrolling lines of Rust code, glowing golden cursor, ultra-clean high frame rate UI

editors.name: JetBrains PyCharm
editors.pricing_details: Community Edition is 100% Free (Open Source). Professional Edition is ~$10-$25/month with Web/Django/Database tools.
editors.target_audience: Python engineers, Data Scientists, Django/FastAPI backend developers
pros: Unrivaled Python deep code analysis, auto-imports, and smart refactoring
Built-in database manager, interactive Jupyter Notebook support, and virtual environment manager
Out-of-the-box support for Django, Flask, FastAPI, and scientific libraries
Robust debugger and test runner
cons: Heavy Java JVM resource usage; can be slow to start on low-end machines
Professional features (Web & DB tooling) require paid license subscription
Steeper learning curve due to dense feature set
editors.best_for: Professional Python developers working on complex data science or full-stack web applications.
editors.visual_theme: JetBrains Darcula dark theme, glowing green Python execution terminal, interactive scientific plot charts on right pane, professional dual-monitor setup

editors.name: Windsurf AI IDE (Cascade)
editors.pricing_details: Free tier with Codeium AI chat; Pro tier at $15-$20/month for advanced Cascade flows.
editors.target_audience: Full-stack developers seeking deep autonomous agent workflows and automated terminal command execution
pros: Cascade AI flow provides deep step-by-step agentic problem solving
Superb understanding of multi-repository relationships and terminal output
Very fast response times powered by Codeium infrastructure
Built on VS Code foundation for seamless extension migration
cons: Cascade flow tokens consume quotas quickly on complex tasks
Newer entry in the market with evolving user interface tweaks
Requires cloud connectivity for AI agent execution
editors.best_for: Developers looking for a true agentic coding assistant that can run terminal commands and write code autonomously.
editors.visual_theme: Futuristic cyan and deep ocean dark aesthetic, glowing animated Cascade AI flow diagram in side panel, automated code edits applying in real time

editors.name: Neovim
editors.target_audience: Keyboard-centric developers, DevOps engineers, Linux enthusiasts, and modal editing purists
pros: Zero mouse dependency; lightning-fast modal editing efficiency
Infinitely customizable using Lua scripts and modern plugin managers (Lazy.nvim)
Built-in Language Server Protocol (LSP) client for rich IDE auto-completions
Runs directly inside terminal with negligible RAM usage (<50MB)
cons: Steep initial learning curve requiring muscle memory for keybindings
Requires effort and time to configure custom setup or distribution (NfVim / LazyVim)
No default GUI out of the box (though Neovide/GUIs exist)
editors.best_for: Developers who want complete keyboard mastery, custom tailored setups, and blisteringly fast editing anywhere.
editors.visual_theme: Retro-modern hacker aesthetic, dark terminal background with glowing violet and neon text, zero UI chrome, matrix-like blazing fast typing speed

editors.name: Sublime Text 4
editors.pricing_details: $99 per license for 3 years of updates; full feature evaluation with occasional pop-up.
editors.target_audience: Developers and writers who prioritize ultra-fast file opening, multi-cursor editing, and minimal resource usage
pros: Instantaneous startup time and file opening even on massive log/code files
GPU accelerated rendering engine for butter-smooth scrolling
Pioneered multi-cursor editing and Goto Anything navigation
Extremely low CPU and RAM consumption
cons: License fee required for continuous nag-free usage
Lacks built-in terminal or deep debugger without custom package setup
Smaller plugin ecosystem compared to VS Code
editors.best_for: Developers needing a dependable, ultra-fast secondary editor or primary minimalist coding tool.
editors.visual_theme: Sleek Monokai dark palette, smooth GPU scrolling, multi-cursor editing highlights across hundreds of lines, high contrast vibrant text
